siteCrawl.title: Site Crawl
siteCrawl.subtitle: Crawl a whole site and audit every URL — broken links, duplicate titles, redirects and indexability
siteCrawl.urlPlaceholder: Enter a URL to crawl, e.g. https://example.com
siteCrawl.stopHint: Ends the crawl but keeps everything found so far
siteCrawl.clearHint: Delete this crawl and its data
siteCrawl.resumableBanner: A crawl of {{url}} was interrupted — you can pick it up where it left off.
siteCrawl.seedRedirectBanner: This URL redirects to {{target}} — the site lives there, so only the redirect itself could be crawled.
siteCrawl.historySubtitle: Every stored crawl — open, resume, re-crawl or delete
siteCrawl.historyEmptyHint: Finished crawls are stored here, ready to reopen any time.
siteCrawl.sizeWarning: Crawl history is using {{size}} — deleting old runs frees space
siteCrawl.confirmDeleteRunBody: The crawl of {{host}} ({{count}} URLs) and all its data will be permanently removed.
siteCrawl.confirmClearHistoryBody: Every stored crawl will be permanently removed, freeing {{size}}.
siteCrawl.dnsBlockedBanner: {{host}} resolved to this computer, so there was nothing to crawl. A public address should never point here — your DNS server is most likely blocking this domain. Try switching your DNS to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8, then run ipconfig /flushdns and crawl again.
siteCrawl.emptyBody: Enter a URL above and press Start — every page found will stream into this table.
siteCrawl.noRowsBody: This view has no URLs yet.
siteCrawl.noRowsFiltered: No URLs match the current filter or search — try widening it.
siteCrawl.clearBody: This removes the crawl and all {{count}} crawled URLs from history. This cannot be undone.
siteCrawl.listHint: One URL per line. The crawler fetches exactly these and follows nothing.
siteCrawl.configHint: One global set of options, applied to the next crawl you start.
siteCrawl.helpMaxDepth: How many links away from the start URL the spider may go. URLs found in sitemaps enter at depth 0, so sitemap discovery can reach beyond this limit.
siteCrawl.helpMaxURLs: The crawl stops queueing new URLs past this count.
siteCrawl.helpDelay: Minimum gap between two requests to the same host. 0 means full speed; the crawler still backs off on 429/503.
siteCrawl.helpCrawlExternal: Fetch external URLs to record their status. Their links are never followed.
siteCrawl.helpCrawlImages: Fetch every to record its status and size — fills the Images tab and finds broken images.
siteCrawl.helpCrawlCSS: Fetch every stylesheet the pages load — fills the CSS filter.
siteCrawl.helpCrawlJS: Fetch every script the pages load — fills the JS filter.
siteCrawl.helpSubdomains: Treat blog.example.com as part of example.com.
siteCrawl.helpUserAgent: How the crawler identifies itself to the site.
siteCrawl.helpThreads: How many requests run at once. Every thread hits the same site, so this is the load your server sees.
siteCrawl.warnThreads: Above 10 threads you may slow down or overload the site you are crawling.
siteCrawl.helpRespectCrawlDelay: Wait the interval robots.txt asks for between requests (capped at 5s). Off by default — it paces every request, so a crawl can drop to one URL per second whatever the thread count.
siteCrawl.helpSitemaps: Seed the crawl from sitemap.xml — this is what finds orphan pages.
siteCrawl.helpIgnoreSSL: Crawl sites with invalid certificates. The pages are still flagged.
siteCrawl.helpUseProxy: Off, the crawl connects directly. On, it uses the proxy saved in Connections, so the site sees that IP instead of yours — expect a slower crawl, since every thread shares the one proxy.
siteCrawl.proxyMissingBody: Crawl through proxy is on but Connections has no proxy, so the crawl will connect directly anyway.
siteCrawl.helpHeaders: One "Name: value" per line, sent with every request.
siteCrawl.helpPatterns: Regular expressions matched against the full URL, one per line.
siteCrawl.helpDefaultExcl: Skip issue reporting on ~200 known utility paths (wp-admin, cart, login…).
siteCrawl.helpExclusions: Path globs (one per line) whose pages never produce issues.
siteCrawl.helpEnableJS: Load pages in a headless Chrome/Edge already installed on this machine, so content added by JavaScript is crawled. Slower — each rendered page costs a browser load.
siteCrawl.helpJSMaxPages: Hard cap on how many pages get the browser treatment; the rest are crawled normally.
siteCrawl.helpJSWait: How long to let scripts settle before reading the page.
siteCrawl.helpJSConcurrency: Concurrent tabs. Each one is a real browser process.
siteCrawl.helpJSPatterns: Regular expressions, one per line. Empty = render every eligible page.
siteCrawl.noBrowserBanner: JavaScript rendering is on, but no Chrome or Edge was found on this machine — pages were crawled without rendering.
siteCrawl.psiKeyBody: The key is free from Google Cloud Console (PageSpeed Insights API). Add it under Connections, where every credential in this app lives.
siteCrawl.psiRunHint: Measures every internal HTML page that has no result yet. Tick rows in the grid first to measure only those. Each page is a full Lighthouse pass on Google's side (~20s).
siteCrawl.psiNothingToMeasure: Every page already has a result for this device.
siteCrawl.psiEmptyBody: Turn on PageSpeed in Configuration to measure during the crawl, or run it here for the pages already crawled.
siteCrawl.psiCruxOrigin: These are the whole domain's numbers — this page alone has too little traffic for Chrome to report on it.
siteCrawl.helpEnablePageSpeed: Every internal HTML page that answers is sent to Google's PageSpeed Insights API while the crawl runs. Results land in the PageSpeed and Opportunities tabs.
siteCrawl.helpPSIStrategy: Mobile and desktop are separate measurements. Switching device later measures every page again for the new one.
siteCrawl.psiSlowWarn: Google takes about 20 seconds per page, so this keeps running after the crawl finishes — roughly 30 minutes for 1,000 pages. It has its own progress bar and Stop button, and everything measured is kept.
siteCrawl.psiConfigNeedsKey: PageSpeed is on but no key is saved, so the crawl will skip the measurements. The key is free from Google Cloud Console.
siteCrawl.oppEmptyBody: Opportunities come from PageSpeed. Run it on this crawl, and the fixes worth making show up here.
siteCrawl.helpDuplication: Group pages with identical titles/descriptions/H1s and find near-copies.
siteCrawl.helpDupThreshold: 0.85 means pages whose title, description, H1 and length are 85% alike count as duplicates.
siteCrawl.paneEmpty: Select a row to see its details.
siteCrawl.paneNoMeta: No meta description — Google will improvise one.
